 Operational revenue growth accelerated to 4% in the third quarter, driven by a doubling of product sales and increased contributions from non-wager-based software services. 
 Management attributed the decline in U.S. same-store sales to exceptionally difficult comparisons against record-breaking multistate jackpots in the prior year rather than a structural shift in player demand. 
 The Italy B2C strategy is transitioning from infrastructure investment to active player engagement, utilizing the MyLotteries PLAY app and Dual Play games to convert retail foot traffic into digital accounts. 
 Success in New Jersey and Indiana reinforces the company's lottery management agreement (LMA) playbook, which utilizes direct operational involvement to drive low to mid-single-digit growth in instant ticket sales. 
 Resilient adjusted EBITDA margins were maintained through the OPtiMa cost-efficiency program, which successfully offset inflationary pressures and ongoing investments in digital growth initiatives. 
 The company is intentionally expanding its 'other service revenue' segment, focusing on recurring software and maintenance fees to build a more predictable revenue base outside of volatile wager-based cycles. 
 Outlook and Strategic Assumptions 
 Full-year revenue and EBITDA guidance were revised downward to account for lower Multistate Jackpot expectations and the strengthening of the U.S. dollar against the euro. 
 Management expects to maintain the 4% operational growth rate in the fourth quarter, supported by the continued phasing of Italy B2C initiatives and scheduled hardware deliveries. 
 The long-term growth algorithm is shifting to prioritize iLottery and Italian B2C services as primary drivers to offset potentially slower retail same-store sales growth. 
 Capital expenditure timing has been rephased, with a portion of 2026 spending moving into 2027 to align with specific project milestones and contract requirements. 
 The company anticipates a 15-month extension of the Italy Scratch & Win contract through 2029, requiring EUR 188 million in payments across two installments in 2027. 
 Operational Risks and Non-Recurring Factors 
 Reported revenue was impacted by a $46 million non-cash amortization charge related to the upfront fee for the new Italy Lotto license. 
 A record-breaking summer heat wave in Italy caused a 2% reduction in retail foot traffic, temporarily dampening lottery sales during the third quarter. 
 October performance in Italy was hindered by a regional trucker strike that delayed the physical delivery of instant tickets to retail outlets, though retailers utilized on-hand inventory to mitigate the impact. 
 Management noted that the Mega Millions game algorithm change has resulted in lower-than-expected player engagement at lower jackpot tiers compared to previous versions.

 Impact of macro factors on U.S. and Italy sales

 Management observed that while lower-income consumers face inflationary pressure, demand for high-price-point instant games ($20-$50) remains robust among higher-end players. 
 The Italy trucker strike caused a temporary delay in ticket deliveries, but the situation is expected to stabilize following government intervention with tax credits for the association. 
 Italy Scratch and Win contract extension and funding 
 The proposed 15-month extension through 2029 would be funded via existing revolver capacity without impacting the company's long-term leverage trajectory. 
 The extension is part of a broader budget law that also introduces a new weekly Lotto draw on Wednesdays to stimulate player interest and revenue. 
 Sustainability of margin expansion and cost-saving initiatives 
 The OPtiMa program has been upgraded to $100 million in total savings, with approximately $10 million in year-over-year benefits expected for 2027. 
 Management is exploring AI-driven business process reengineering as the next phase of operational efficiency beyond the current program's 2028 conclusion. 
 Long-term revenue growth algorithm and terminal growth rates 
 Management reaffirmed a 5% CAGR target, though the mix is shifting toward 20% recurring growth in iLottery to offset slower retail same-store sales. 
 Profitability for new digital initiatives is expected to scale following an initial heavy investment period typical of B2C launches.
